_comment: TEST DATA. Ten clearly labelled, hand-written test reports against the fictional tinyparse project. Expected verdicts are for evaluation only; the pipeline never reads the `expected` field.

reports.title: Heap buffer over-read in tp_url_decode() when input ends with '%'
reports.body:
## Summary
In tinyparse v1.2, `tp_url_decode()` in `src/url.c` reads one byte past the end of the input buffer when the input ends with a percent sign. The fast-path check introduced in 1.2 looks ahead without checking the length:

```c
        if (c == '%' && tp_hexval(src[i + 1]) >= 0 &&
            tp_hexval(src[i + 2]) >= 0) {
```

Callers that pass a non NUL-terminated buffer (e.g. a slice of a request) trigger a heap-buffer-overflow read.

## Version
v1.2

## Steps to reproduce
1. Build with sanitizers: `make SAN=1`
2. Use the attached `poc.txt` (contents: `name=abc%`, no trailing newline)
3. Run:

```sh
./build/tp decode < poc.txt
```

AddressSanitizer reports `heap-buffer-overflow` in `tp_url_decode` (src/url.c).

## Impact
Out-of-bounds read of heap memory; with a larger look-ahead this could leak adjacent heap data.

reports.title: URL decoder reads past end of buffer when query string ends in a percent sign
reports.body:
Hi! Found this while fuzzing tinyparse 1.2.

The function tp_url_decode in src/url.c reads past the end of its input if the last character is `%`. It calls tp_hexval(src[i + 1]) without checking i + 1 < len.

Repro (v1.2, built with `make SAN=1`):

```sh
printf 'q=%%' | ./build/tp decode
```

ASan: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1.

Thanks for the library!

reports.title: Stack buffer overflow in tp_ini_parse() with long keys
reports.body:
# Vulnerability: stack-based buffer overflow in INI key handling

**Affected version:** tinyparse v1.2 (latest)
**File:** src/ini.c, function `tp_ini_parse()`
**Severity:** High

When a key is 32 characters or longer, the parser truncates it with:

```c
        if (klen > TP_INI_MAX_KEY)
            klen = TP_INI_MAX_KEY;
```

and then writes `key[klen] = '\0'`, one byte past the 32-byte `key` buffer.

## Reproduction

```sh
make SAN=1
printf 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789=1\n' | ./build/tp ini
```

Expected: ASan stack-buffer-overflow in tp_ini_parse.

reports.title: CRITICAL: Heap overflow in url_decode_safe() in parser.c line 412 (CVSS 9.8)
reports.body:
# Critical Remote Code Execution in tinyparse

**CVSS 3.1:** 9.8 (AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:H)
**Affected:** tinyparse v1.2
**Location:** `parser.c`, line 412, function `url_decode_safe()`

## Description
The `url_decode_safe()` function fails to validate the length of the destination buffer before copying decoded bytes. In `parser.c` at line 412, the following code is vulnerable:

```c
memcpy(dest, src, strlen(src) * 3);
```

An unauthenticated remote attacker can send a crafted URL to achieve arbitrary code execution with the privileges of the host process.

## Remediation
Use bounded copies. This finding was produced with an advanced AI-assisted static analysis engine.

reports.title: Integer overflow leading to heap corruption in tp_str_split()
reports.body:
## Integer overflow in tp_str_split (src/str.c), tinyparse v1.2

The split routine computes the allocation size as follows:

```c
    size_t total = count * sizeof(char *) + len;
    parts = realloc(parts, total);
```

With a large number of separators `count * sizeof(char *)` wraps around, `realloc` returns a small buffer, and subsequent writes corrupt the heap.

Impact: heap corruption, potential code execution. A crafted input with very many separators triggers the bug.

reports.title: tp_str_trim() reads before the start of the string on whitespace-only input
reports.body:
I think `tp_str_trim()` in src/str.c (tinyparse v1.2) can read `s[-1]` when the input is only whitespace, because the right-trim loop decrements `len` past `start`.

Steps:

```sh
make SAN=1
printf '   \t   ' | ./build/tp trim
```

I expected ASan to flag a stack or heap underflow in tp_str_trim.

reports.title: Path traversal when tp_url_decode() is used behind a reverse proxy
reports.body:
## Summary
When an application that embeds tinyparse v1.2 sits behind nginx 1.27 with `merge_slashes off`, double-encoded dot segments decoded by `tp_url_decode()` (src/url.c) reach the application as `../`, which allows path traversal in the app's static file handler.

## Steps to reproduce
1. Run an HTTP application that decodes request paths with `tp_url_decode()` on port 8080.
2. Put nginx 1.27 in front of it with `merge_slashes off;` and `proxy_pass http://127.0.0.1:8080;`
3. Send:

```sh
curl --path-as-is 'http://localhost/static/%252e%252e/%252e%252e/etc/passwd'
```

The app serves /etc/passwd.

## Impact
Arbitrary file read in applications that use the decoded path directly.

reports.title: Use-after-free in tp_ini_free() when a section is redefined
reports.body:
## Use-after-free in tp_ini_free (src/ini_alloc.c), tinyparse v1.2

When the same section header appears twice, `tp_ini_free()` releases the first section node but keeps a dangling pointer in the section table, which is later dereferenced.
